name: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017
usage: General and code, very large MoE; on 128 GB only with SSD streaming or 1-bit

sources.note: IQ2_XXS-Q2_K, 366 GB (152 GiB weights + 189 GiB Engram tables), for DwarfStar with SSD streaming
UD-IQ1_S, 233 GB (122 GB weights + 111 GB Engram file with extension .gguf_file), for llama.cpp
IQ1_M 121 GB / IQ2_XXS 138 GB, plus 111 GB Engram file; llama.cpp >= b11870
V4.1-Flash of 10.09.2026; 1017 is a minor update of it

release_date.note: createdAt of the repository; minor update of V4.1-Flash (10.09.2026)

parameters_total_b.note: 552B backbone plus 196B Engram n-gram tables (Unsloth guide); activated parameters not stated; 384 experts, 6 active per token

size_gb.note: GGUF sizes include the Engram tables, which are read from disk (mmap)

languages.value: multilingual (not detailed in the card); built-in vision

runtimes.value: DwarfStar (ds4, Metal, vision; on 128 GB only with --ssd-streaming; open issues #1235 checksum, #1335 stuck read, #1330 Metal memory growth); llama.cpp since PR #31086 (open #31385 Flash-1017 GGUF problems, #30944 output corruption with cached prefix); MLX: mlx-community oQ2.5e (423 GB) or a pruned community build; Ollama: cloud tags only; Strata (MIT; separate DeepSeek engine with Metal, CUDA, HIP and Strix Halo builds; experts streamed from the SSD; ISTA-DASLab 1.75–2.25 bpw sets of 239–274 GB on disk)
runtimes.note: llama.cpp performance on Metal with the Engram mmap, and the 2-bit SSD-streaming speed on an M5 Max 128 GB, are unverified. Strata's own measurement on an M5 Max 128 GB (2.00 bpw, build 0.2.7.1, another model loaded at the same time): 15–18 tok/s on a short question, a 3,000-token prompt in about 11 s, about 68 GB of experts kept in memory; context above 32K not measured (checked 15.11.2026)

fits_128gb.note: no build is resident in 128 GB; runs with SSD streaming (DwarfStar 2-bit) or at 1 bit (Unsloth UD-IQ1_S, ISTA-DASLab IQ1_M); the Engram tables are always read from disk

web.verdict: Praised as much better than V4, mostly through APIs; on 128 GB only by SSD streaming or 1-bit
web.summary: Users find it far better than V4 Flash and close to frontier models on well-defined tasks, but nearly all of that is API use. Local reports on 128 GB Macs are few: usable but behind Codex and Claude, coherent at 1 bit, some looping at 2 bit. No local report on tool calling.
web.scope: Released 17.10.2026: all comments since release. Hacker News comments (Algolia API), Hugging Face discussions, GitHub issues (ds4, llama.cpp); Reddit blocked.

comments.text: Feels much better than V4 Flash ([liuliu, 07.11.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50405607)); far better than V4, with about twice the parameters, and on par with Opus 5.5 on well-defined tasks, local or API not stated ([sjbzbeiks, 07.11.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50408642)).

Found a community Ollama build of 0731 almost useless; very happy with the Unsloth GGUF of 1017 for coding, quantisation and hardware not stated ([ericpruitt, 07.11.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50409154)).

Tested V4 and V4.1 Flash locally on an M5 Mac Studio with 128 GB: both useful, but they need steering and retries and are well behind Codex and Claude ([davedx, 12.11.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50470346)).

An IQ1 quant was coherent and of good quality once the runtime settings were fixed; a reply reports looping with a Q2 build ([latentsea and ferroman, 09–11.11.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50422422)).

Runs on 128 GB and more with Unsloth's SSD offloading, no figures ([selcuka, 06.11.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50386477)). V4.1-Flash (before 1017) at 4 bits streamed from SSD on an M5 Max 128 GB: about 14 tok/s decode, from a self-promoting source ([Argonautlabs, 15.09.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49712330)).

Communicates less well than Google models, API use ([bscphil, 10.11.2026](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50442722)). Garbled replies in non-thinking mode ([HF #33](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/discussions/33)) and overthinking ([HF #29](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/discussions/29)).

MLX on an M3 Ultra 256 GB uses about 204 GB of memory ([HF #78](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017/discussions/78)); Q4 SSD-streaming decode about 8–9 tok/s on a 256 GB M3 Ultra ([ds4 #1085, 18.09.2026](https://github.com/antirez/ds4/issues/1085)).
